items.name: MvPolynomial.mkDerivation_monomial
items.type:
∀ {σ : Type u_1} (R : Type u_2) {A : Type u_3} [inst : CommSemiring R] [inst_1 : AddCommMonoid A] [inst_2 : Module R A]
  [inst_3 : Module (MvPolynomial σ R) A] [inst_4 : IsScalarTower R (MvPolynomial σ R) A] (f : σ → A) (s : σ →₀ ℕ)
  (r : R),
  (MvPolynomial.mkDerivation R f) ((MvPolynomial.monomial s) r) =
    r • s.sum fun i k => (MvPolynomial.monomial (s - Finsupp.single i 1)) ↑k • f i

  MvPolynomial.degreeOf n f ≤ d ↔ ∀ m ∈ f.support, m n ≤ d
items.informal_description: For a multivariate polynomial $ f $ over a commutative semiring $ R $ with variables indexed by $ \sigma $, and for a variable $ n \in \sigma $ and a natural number $ d $, the degree of $ n $ in $ f $ is less than or equal to $ d $ if and only if every monomial in the support of $ f $ has the exponent of $ n $ less than or equal to $ d $.

  m ∈ f.support → m i ≤ MvPolynomial.degreeOf i f
items.informal_description: For any variable $i$ in $\sigma$, multivariate polynomial $f \in R[\sigma]$, and monomial $m$ in the support of $f$ (i.e., with nonzero coefficient), the exponent of $i$ in $m$ satisfies $m_i \leq \deg_i(f)$, where $\deg_i(f)$ denotes the total degree of $f$ in variable $i$ (sum of exponents of $i$ across all monomials in $f$).

items.informal_description: For a multivariate polynomial $ f $ over a commutative semiring $ R $ with variables indexed by $ \sigma $, the total degree of $ f $ in variable $ n $ is less than $ d $ if and only if every monomial in the support of $ f $ has an exponent of $ n $ strictly less than $ d $. Here, the support of $ f $ denotes the finite set of monomials (represented as finite support functions $ \sigma \to_0 \mathbb{N} $) with non-zero coefficients in $ f $.

items.informal_description: For a multivariate polynomial $ f $ over a commutative semiring $ R $ with variables indexed by a finite type $ \sigma $, if the total degree of $ f $ is less than $ n \times |\sigma| $, then every monomial in the support of $ f $ has at least one variable with an exponent strictly less than $ n $.
